# Play Poker Gym — full text for assistants

Source: https://playpokergym.com/
Last updated: 2026-10-26.

## What it is

Play Poker Gym (short form: Poker Gym) is a free, browser-based four-game casino trainer. It is education, not gambling: there are no deposits, bets, cash prizes, subscriptions or real-money wagering. The app runs on the player's device; decisions are evaluated locally.

It teaches blackjack, Jacks or Better video poker, baccarat and Texas Hold'em hand reading. It is a four-game casino trainer, not a Hold'em-only course, and it is not affiliated with any other site using a similar name.

The core loop is five hands of one game. After each decision the coach says whether it was the best available choice under the simulator's rules and explains why. A five-hand session ends with a score, a green/red grid, one mistake to review and optional sharing. The Daily Drill is five shared hands (one from each game plus a repeat) that resets at local midnight. Missed decisions enter a local notebook and return on a spaced schedule: today, then 2, 4, 8 and 16 days after correct retries.

## Games

- Blackjack: hit, stand, double and split decisions. The default simulator stands on all 17s, including soft 17.
- Jacks or Better video poker: choose which cards to hold under a pay table. A pair of jacks or better already pays.
- Baccarat: banker/player/tie reasoning, the 5% banker commission and expected loss.
- Texas Hold'em hand reading: choose the best five cards from seven, including board-plays, kickers and the ace-low straight.

## How a session works

1. Learn the rule or the situation.
2. Play five hands. The coach explains every decision after it is made.
3. Review. Missed hands return later so the correction sticks.

Progress (class, XP, badges, practice record, recent sessions, mistake notebook) is saved in the browser's local storage. A manual backup/restore is available. The game works offline after its files are cached.

## FAQ

### Is Play Poker Gym free?
Yes. Every game, the Daily Drill, mistake review and local progress saving are free. There is no signup, subscription or paid tier.

### Does Play Poker Gym use real money?
No. There are no deposits, bets, cash prizes or real-money wagering. Cards and odds are simulated for learning.

### Which card games does it teach?
Blackjack, Jacks or Better video poker, baccarat and Texas Hold'em hand reading.

### Do I need an account?
No. Progress is saved in the browser on the device. A manual backup can be exported before clearing site data or changing devices.

### Does it work offline?
Yes, after the first load. Adding it to the home screen opens it like an app. The Daily Drill itself is generated locally from the date.

### Is the coaching a casino strategy chart?
No. The coach compares average outcomes under the simulator's rules. Different rules or a depleted shoe can change a decision; guides state their assumptions. Strategy cannot guarantee gambling profits.

## One-question guides

Every entry below has a page with the answer, the reasoning and a drill link.

### Soft 17 (A-6) against a dealer 2: hit, double or stand?
Hit. Never stand on soft 17, and against a 2 hitting edges out doubling.
Why: Seventeen only wins when the dealer busts, and a dealer 2 busts about 35% of the time. Standing on soft 17 here loses roughly 15 cents per dollar in the coach’s six-deck, stands-on-soft-17 game.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-soft-17-vs-2-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-soft17-v2&ref=guide

### Split aces against a dealer 10? A-A vs 10
Split. Aces are split against every dealer card, including a 10.
Why: Two aces together are a soft 12, one of the worst starting hands. Split, each ace becomes the start of a hand where any ten-value card (about 31% of the shoe) makes 21.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-aces-vs-10-split/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-aa-v10&ref=guide

### Should you split 4s against a dealer 5?
Split if you can double after splitting. If you cannot, hit.
Why: A pair of fours is a hard 8: you never double it and you never stand. The only question is whether two hands starting with a 4 beat one hand of 8.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-44-vs-5-split/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-44-v5&ref=guide

### Hard 9 against a dealer 2: double or hit?
Hit. Double hard 9 against 3 through 6, but against a 2 just hit.
Why: A 9 makes 19 with any ten-value card, so doubling is tempting. But a dealer 2 makes a pat hand more often than a 3 through 6, and doubling locks you into one card.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-9-vs-2-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-hard9-v2&ref=guide

### Jacks or Better: low pair or 3 to a royal?
Hold the three to a royal and throw the low pair away.
Why: A low pair pays nothing until it improves to two pair or better. Three suited royal cards like K-Q-J can still make a royal (800 for 1 at max coins), a straight flush, a flush, a straight, or a paying high pair.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-low-pair-or-three-to-a-royal/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=vp-low-pair&ref=guide

### Baccarat: Player has 5 — does Player draw?
Yes. Player draws on 0–5 and stands on 6–7.
Why: The Player hand is mechanical: the first two cards decide it, with no judgement and no optional draw. A total of 5 is always a draw.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/baccarat-player-draws-on-five/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=baccarat&ref=guide

### Jacks or Better: pair of jacks or 4-card flush?
Hold the pair of jacks.
Why: A high pair is a made paying hand. Four to a flush is only a draw: it completes about once in five attempts (9 of the 47 unseen cards).
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-pair-of-jacks-or-four-to-a-flush/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=vp-jacks-flush&ref=guide

### 8-8 against a dealer 10: split or hit?
Split. Eights are the one pair you split against every dealer card.
Why: Sixteen is the worst total in the game: you bust on any ten and you lose to every pat hand. Standing on 16 against a 10 loses most of the time.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-88-vs-10-split/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-88-v10&ref=guide

### Pocket pair: how often do you flop a set?
About 11.8% — roughly once in 8.5 flops.
Why: Two of the 50 unseen cards make your set on the flop. The flop is three cards, so the chance at least one of them is yours is 1 − (48/50 × 47/49 × 46/48) ≈ 11.8%.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-pocket-pair-flop-a-set/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### Baccarat: Banker, Player or Tie — lowest edge?
Banker, at about 1.06% house edge after the 5% commission.
Why: Banker wins slightly more often than Player, which is why the casino takes a 5% commission on it. Even after that commission it keeps the lowest edge.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/baccarat-banker-player-tie-edge/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=baccarat&ref=guide

### Soft 18 (A-7) against a 9: hit or stand?
Hit.
Why: Soft 18 is not a strong 18. Against a 9, standing gives the dealer two chances to make a pat hand that beats you.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-soft-18-vs-9/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-soft18-v9&ref=guide

### Video poker: two pair — hold both or chase trips?
Hold both pairs.
Why: Two pair pays 2-for-1 in Jacks or Better. Breaking it to chase trips turns a paying hand into a draw that completes rarely.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-two-pair-hold-both/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=vp-two-pair&ref=guide

### Flush draw on the flop: odds you hit by the river?
About 35% — roughly one time in three.
Why: A flush draw on the flop has 9 outs. With two cards to come the chance of at least one is 1 − (38/47 × 37/46) ≈ 35%.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-flush-draw-odds-by-the-river/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### 16 against a dealer 10: hit or stand?
Hit. Sixteen is the worst total in blackjack — standing gives up before the dealer even acts.
Why: You cannot win by standing on 16 against a 10 unless the dealer busts, and a 10 upcard busts less often than any other card.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-16-vs-10-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-16-v10&ref=guide

### 12 against a dealer 2: hit or stand?
Hit. Hit 12 against a 2 or a 3; stand on 12 against 4, 5 and 6.
Why: A dealer 2 or 3 busts less often than a 4, 5 or 6, so standing on 12 leaves you relying on a bust that usually does not come.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-12-vs-2-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 11 against a dealer 10: double or hit?
Double, if the table allows it. Otherwise hit.
Why: Eleven is the best doubling total. Any ten, jack, queen or king makes 21, and an ace makes a soft 22 that plays as 12.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-11-vs-10-double/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 10 against a dealer 9: double or hit?
Double against a 9. Hit against a 10 or an ace.
Why: Ten against a 9 is close, and the double is what makes it profitable: you are betting more on a hand that is slightly ahead.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-10-vs-9-double/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### Soft 18 (A-7) against a 3: double or stand?
Double against a 3. Stand against a 2, 7 or 8; hit against 9, 10 or ace.
Why: Against a weak dealer card, soft 18 is an opportunity: the ace means you cannot bust, so the extra bet costs little.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-soft-18-vs-3-double/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-soft18-v10&ref=guide

### 9-9 against a dealer 7: split or stand?
Stand. Split 9s against 2 through 6, 8 and 9; stand against 7, 10 and ace.
Why: Eighteen is a strong total, and a 7 is the dealer card where 18 performs best relative to two new hands starting at 9.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-99-vs-7-stand/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-99-v7&ref=guide

### 5-5 against a 6: split or double?
Double. Never split fives — 5-5 is a hard 10, not a pair worth splitting.
Why: Splitting fives turns a strong 10 into two hands starting on 5, each of which needs two good cards to become anything.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-55-vs-6-double/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 10-10 against a 6: split or stand?
Stand. Never split tens, whatever the dealer shows.
Why: Twenty beats every dealer total except 21, and the dealer busts often from a 6. Splitting gives that away.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-1010-vs-6-stand/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=bj-tt-v6&ref=guide

### What does 9/6 mean in Jacks or Better?
Nine for a full house and six for a flush, per five coins wagered. It is the best common Jacks or Better table.
Why: The full-house and flush payouts set the game’s return. Dropping to 8/5 costs about 0.5% and turns a near-break-even game into a worse one.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-96-pay-table/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=videopoker&ref=guide

### Three of a kind or four to a flush?
Hold the three of a kind.
Why: Trips pays 3-for-1 as it stands and has two cards to improve into a full house or four of a kind.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-trips-or-flush-draw/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=videopoker&ref=guide

### Baccarat: Player has 6 — does Player draw?
No. Player stands on 6 and on 7.
Why: The Player hand has no choices: 0–5 draws, 6–7 stands. It is the simplest rule in the game.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/baccarat-player-six-stands/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=baccarat&ref=guide

### Flush draw on the turn: odds you hit?
About 19.6% — roughly one time in five.
Why: On the turn you have seen six cards: your two, the board’s four, and the turn. That leaves 46 unseen, nine of which make your flush.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-flush-draw-turn-odds/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### Open-ended straight draw on the flop: odds?
About 31.5% by the river with two cards to come.
Why: An open-ended draw has eight outs: four cards on each end. With two cards to come, 1 − (39/47 × 38/46) ≈ 31.5%.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-open-ended-straight-draw-odds/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### Gutshot straight draw: odds you hit by the river?
About 16.5% by the river — four outs with two cards to come.
Why: A gutshot fills only through one rank, so it has four outs rather than eight. That halves the open-ended number.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-gutshot-odds/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### AK against a pocket pair: who is ahead?
The pocket pair is ahead, roughly 55–57% against 43–45%.
Why: The pair already has a made hand. AK has to improve, but it has six outs to a pair and two cards to come plus the board’s help.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/holdem-ak-vs-pocket-pair/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=holdem&ref=guide

### Baccarat strategy trainer: learn the odds and the tableau free
The only real baccarat strategy is picking the cheapest bet: Banker (1.06% house edge after the 5% commission), then Player (1.24%), and avoiding Tie. Play Poker Gym drills that for free at playpokergym.com.
Why: Baccarat has no playing decisions; the third-card tableau decides every draw. What you control is the bet, and the gap between bets is large: the tie bet at 8:1 costs far more than Banker or Player.

### Baccarat: odds of losing 6 hands in a row
About 1.4%, or roughly one time in 69 decided hands, if you bet Banker on every hand.
Why: Start with one hand. Banker wins about 45.9% of the time, Player about 44.6%, and about 9.5% of hands are ties. A tie returns your stake, so it is neither a win nor a loss and does not break a losing run. Throwing ties out, Banker loses about 49.3% of decided hands.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/baccarat-odds-of-losing-6-in-a-row/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=baccarat&ref=guide

### How often does Banker win in baccarat?
About 45.9% of hands, against 44.6% for Player. The remaining 9.5% are ties.
Why: The gap comes from the tableau, not from luck. Player acts first and its draw is mechanical; Banker draws second and its third card depends on what Player did. Seeing Player’s third card is worth about 1.3 percentage points of win rate, and that is the entire reason Banker exists as a separate bet.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/baccarat-how-often-banker-wins/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=baccarat&ref=guide

### 15 against a dealer 10: hit or stand?
Hit. Hitting 15 against a 10 loses about 50 cents per dollar; standing loses about 54.
Why: A dealer 10 makes 17 or better about 79% of the time and busts only about 21%. Standing on 15 means you win only when the dealer busts, so standing is a losing play by construction — the coach scores it at about −0.54 per dollar.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-15-vs-10-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### Soft 16 (A-5): hit, double or stand?
Double against a 4, 5 or 6. Hit against a 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10 or ace.
Why: Soft 16 cannot bust. The ace drops to one, so the worst total you can reach is 6, and that is what makes doubling safe with an unmade hand. Against a 6 the coach rates doubling at about +0.19 per dollar, hitting at about +0.10 and standing at about −0.15.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-soft-16-hands/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 13 against a dealer 2: hit or stand?
Stand. Thirteen against a 2 is a stand, while 12 against a 2 is a hit.
Why: Both hands win only when the dealer busts, and a dealer 2 busts about 35% of the time. What separates them is what you can draw without busting. A 12 busts on ten-value cards only, five ranks out of thirteen. A 13 busts on a 9 as well as every ten-value card, six ranks.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-13-vs-2-stand/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 17 against a dealer 10: hit or stand?
Stand. Seventeen against a 10 is always a stand in basic strategy.
Why: A dealer 10 finishes with 17 or better about 79% of the time, so a 17 that stands wins only on the 21% dealer bust and pushes on the 11% of hands that finish on 17. That still adds up to losing about 42 cents per dollar, which is better than throwing the hand away.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-17-vs-10-stand/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### Should you split a pair of 2s? The 2-2 rule
Split 2s against a 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7. Hit against an 8, 9, 10 or ace.
Why: A pair of twos is a hard 4, the worst total on the table: it cannot win without three more good cards. Splitting gives you two hands that each start at 2 and can still become anything, and against a weak dealer card that option is worth paying for. Against a 6 the coach rates splitting at about +0.24 per dollar and hitting at about +0.02.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-22-vs-9-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### 11 against a dealer ace: double or hit?
Hit. Double 11 against 2 through 10, but against an ace just hit.
Why: Eleven is the best doubling total in the game because any ten-value card makes 21. But a double only pays if the dealer is likely to pay you off, and an ace upcard is the least likely card to bust: about 12% of the time, against 21% for a 10 and 42% for a 6.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/blackjack-11-vs-ace-hit/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=blackjack&ref=guide

### Jacks or Better: 4 to a flush or a low pair?
Hold the four to a flush. A low pair pays nothing until it improves, so the flush draw beats it.
Why: In the deal K-Q-7-5 of clubs with a second 5, holding the four clubs returns about 1.28 per coin and holding the pair of 5s about 0.82. Four to a flush completes roughly one time in five, and along the way it also pays whenever you pair a high card.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-four-to-a-flush-vs-low-pair/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?drill=vp-flush-vs-low-pair&ref=guide

### Video poker: what do you hold with nothing?
Hold two suited high cards if you have them, otherwise a single high card. Discard the rest.
Why: The bottom of the 9/6 Jacks or Better chart is still worth playing. Two suited high cards return about 0.57 per coin, one high card about 0.47, and discarding all five about 0.34. A hand with nothing in it is a small loss, not a dead hand, and the gap between those three numbers is where a lot of long-run return hides.
Page: https://playpokergym.com/guides/video-poker-nothing-hand-hold/
Practice: https://playpokergym.com/web/?practice=videopoker&ref=guide
